draft.title: Socialisation
card: Socialisation is the process of learning the norms and values of a society. Through it, people learn what is expected of them and what the people around them think is important.
It begins in early childhood, when a child learns language and basic behaviour from the people who care for them.
It does not stop after childhood. People are socialised again when they start a new school, take a job, move to a new country or become a parent.
Socialisation shapes how people think and act. Two people raised in different societies may respond very differently to the same situation.
draft.remember: Socialisation is learning a society's ways, and it goes on for life.

opts: A new apprentice learns how to behave on a worksite
A child is born with brown hair like her mother
A student memorises dates for a history test
A man buys a car after saving for two years
a.why: The apprentice is learning what is expected in a new setting, which is learning the norms of a group. Memorising dates is learning, but it is not about how to behave or what to value.
a.clue: Look for learning how to behave, not just learning facts.

b.q: Priya moved from Mumbai to Perth at 35 and began to notice how coworkers greeted each other and what they joked about. She started to copy them. What does this show?
opts: Socialisation continues in adult life
Socialisation ends once childhood is over
Socialisation only happens within the family
Socialisation is something people can avoid
b.why: Priya is learning the expected behaviour of a new workplace and society as an adult, so socialisation is lifelong. It is not limited to childhood, which is the tempting wrong answer, because people are socialised again in new settings.
b.clue: Think about when socialisation starts and when it stops.
